[[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] congressman [[John Curtis]] won his first term in office, succeeding Republican incumbent [[Mitt Romney]], who did not seek a second term.{{Cite web|url=https://www.cookpolitical.com/analysis/senate/utah-senate/romney-wont-run-reelection-opening-gop-primary-fight|title=Romney Won't Run for Reelection, Opening GOP Primary Fight|date=September 13, 2023|website=Cook Political}} Utah has been represented in the U.S. Senate exclusively by Republicans since 1977. Despite finishing a distant second behind Riverton mayor [[Trent Staggs]] at the Utah Republican convention, Curtis won the Republican primary with 49% of the vote over Staggs and former state House speaker [[Brad Wilson (politician)|Brad Wilson]].
